root.name: King's Indian Defense: Four Pawns Attack

overview: White builds a four-pawn centre (c4, d4, e4, f4) and gains space, aiming for e5 or a quick attack. Black castles and strikes with ...c5, ...Na6 or ...Nc6 and ...e5, using the fianchettoed bishop to attack d4. With 7.d5 (Dynamic Attack) the game turns into a Benoni-like fight where White pushes e5 and Black counters on the queenside. Both sides can go wrong quickly.

white_ideas.idea: Nf3, Be2, O-O and e5 with a central space advantage
d5 and e5 to cramp Black, with a kingside attack supported by f4

black_ideas.idea: ...c5 or ...Na6 and ...c5 to attack d4 and exploit the extended centre
...Nc6 and ...e5, or ...Bg4 to pin and pressure d4

typical_structures.structure: White c4, d4, e4, f4 pawns against Black d6, g6 and the g7 bishop; Benoni-type after d5

character.notes: Dynamic and double-edged: if Black's counterplay arrives first the centre collapses; if White's e5 works Black is squashed.

gambit.notes: No material offered in main lines.

soundness.notes: Sound for both; considered good enough for Black.

structure.notes: Centre tension with ...c5; not locked in the main line.

approach.notes: A standard White set-up against the KID.

level.notes: Forcing lines and tough strategic decisions for Black.

sublines_that_differ.name: Four Pawns: Dynamic Attack
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. f4 O-O 6. Nf3 c5 7. d5
sublines_that_differ.how: A Benoni-style fight with White's centre against Black's queenside play.

character.reason: Both sides attack, one side collapses fast.

structure.reason: Centre in tension, not yet locked; could be semi-open after ...cxd4.

approach.reason: A standard White set-up against the KID.

level.reason: Forcing theory and hard strategic decisions.

plans.reason: White takes space, Black attacks the centre from the flanks.
